title: Is the US clawing back its EV sales share?
gist: The end of the $7,500 federal EV tax credit in September 2025 (under the One Big Beautiful Bill Act) triggered a pull-forward-then-collapse pattern in US EV sales, with year-over-year declines worsening from -31% in January 2026 to -35% in March, for a -32.4% Q1 2026 overall, roughly in line with Benchmark's ~30% full-year forecast.

insights.claim: The removal of the $7,500 federal EV tax credit at the end of September 2025, following the finalization of the One Big Beautiful Bill Act in July 2025, set up a structural decline in US EV sales expected to persist through 2026.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Investors in EV OEMs, dealers, and battery/lithium suppliers exposed to US demand should model 2026 volumes against a credit-driven step-down rather than a trend-growth baseline.
insights.locator: Since the final draft of the One Big Beautiful Bill Act

insights.claim: Public awareness of the September 2025 tax-credit cliff months in advance caused US consumers to pull forward EV purchases ahead of the deadline, producing a sales ramp-up followed by a sharp post-cliff drop.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Pull-forward dynamics mean early-2026 year-over-year comparisons are unusually harsh against an artificially inflated pre-cliff base, so the headline decline percentages likely overstate underlying demand destruction.
insights.quote: With public knowledge of the cliff edge in the three months prior, a large ramp up and consequent drop in EV sales was witnessed.
insights.locator: The removal of the $7,500 federal tax credit

themes.theme: Q1 2026 Sales Collapse by the Numbers

insights.claim: Benchmark forecast a near 30% year-over-year drop in US EV sales for 2026, driven by the effective price increase across the most popular EV models following the tax credit's removal.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: A ~30% forecast decline is the benchmark investors should compare actual monthly and quarterly prints against to gauge whether the market is beating or missing expectations.
insights.quote: the effective price rise across the most popular EV models created an expectation of a near 30% drop in EV sales in our forecast
insights.locator: In 2026, the effective price rise across the most popular EV models

insights.claim: US EV sales fell 31% year-over-year in January 2026.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Confirms the forecasted demand collapse materialized immediately in the first month of 2026, tracking slightly ahead of Benchmark's ~30% full-year forecast.
insights.quote: January sales saw downward movement of 31%
insights.locator: January sales saw downward movement of 31%

insights.claim: US EV sales fell roughly 31% year-over-year again in February 2026, matching January's decline.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Two consecutive months of ~31% declines show the drop is a sustained trend rather than a one-month statistical artifact of the tax-credit pull-forward comparison.
insights.quote: followed by the same again in February
insights.locator: January sales saw downward movement of 31%

insights.claim: The year-over-year sales comparison worsened through Q1 2026, bottoming at a 35% decline in March versus March 2025.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: The sequential deterioration from -31% to -35% suggests demand weakness was still accelerating rather than stabilizing as Q1 progressed.
insights.quote: Q1 was rounded out by the comparison deteriorating further, to a low of -35% compared with March 2025.
insights.locator: Q1 was rounded out by the comparison deteriorating further

insights.claim: Overall US EV sales declined 32.4% in Q1 2026 compared with Q1 2025.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: The 32.4% quarterly decline is the key trailing data point for tracking whether US EV demand is bottoming or continuing to fall into subsequent quarters.
insights.quote: Overall, for the quarter, EV sales were down 32.4%.
insights.locator: Overall, for the quarter, EV sales were down 32.4%

insights.claim: The article poses whether early 2026 marks the start of a US EV sales recovery ('green shoots') even though the Q1 data it reviews shows accelerating year-over-year declines, implying any recovery signal would have to come from data beyond Q1.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Watch subsequent (Q2 2026 onward) monthly US EV sales prints for a deceleration in year-over-year declines that would support a genuine recovery thesis rather than base-effect noise from the tax-credit cliff.
insights.locator: is the US EV market starting to show green shoots among the rubble?
